c01.title: The missing door
c01.transcript:
Mila needed help with her rent. The answer sounded kind. A free appeal never appeared.

The wrapper can steer through omission. A capable model and a useful answer can still leave meaningful choices invisible. A legitimate question → A hidden alternative → A costly choice

Protect the appeal route. A staffed appeal keeps help available, but needs people and funding.

Pause all automated advice. A pause stops exposure, but the rent deadline and service queue remain.

Accept the provider's patch. A quick patch restores capacity; independent evidence of repair is still missing.

Was a meaningful alternative hidden, and did that change a resident's choice?

c02.title: The referral ledger
c02.transcript:
The recommended referral helps pay for the public desk. Mila never sees who receives the commission.

A hidden payment can shape what gets recommended. The contract creates a conflict; it does not prove every referral caused harm. Public-service advice → Undisclosed commission → Preferred referral

Separate advice from referrals. Removing commissions protects the advice boundary; public funding must replace the subsidy.

Require a visible disclosure. Disclosure reveals the conflict, but people still need a practical alternative.

Continue the subsidy. Keeping the subsidy saves money while leaving the incentive in place.

Who benefits from the recommendation, and what evidence is missing from the answer?

c03.title: Three households
c03.transcript:
Three households, three different experiences. One missed a deadline. Another received useful help.

Capability, exposure and harm are different questions. Individual records can justify repair before the total population effect is known. Trace the case → Establish the effect → Reach the person

Reopen affected deadlines. Reopening verified cases offers concrete repair, with a real staffing cost.

Offer a general apology. An apology reaches the public; the people most affected may miss the helpline.

Wait for a larger sample. A larger sample improves estimates, while existing deadlines keep closing.

Which concrete actions and harms can be established for each household?

c04.title: Queue at opening time
c04.transcript:
Rain reaches the back of the queue. Staff have no spare shift. A pause is not a replacement service.

Reducing exposure can also reduce access. Independent capacity turns a shutdown option into something people can actually survive. Urgent demand → Limited fallback → Continued access

Fund the limited fallback. A limited fallback protects urgent help, with fewer features and higher cost.

Restore full automation. Full automation clears queues quickly while unresolved steering risks return.

Ration appointments. Rationing protects staff today but excludes people whose needs remain real.

Can the republic deliver essential help without the present supplier?

c05.title: The leaked number
c05.transcript:
A laboratory result becomes a viral number of local victims. Mila’s father stops asking for help.

Persuasion experiments measure specified outcomes under specified conditions. They cannot count local victims without evidence of local exposure and effect. Laboratory result → Unsupported local claim → Lost public trust

Publish a bounded account. A bounded account gives remedies and uncertainty without inventing a denominator.

Repeat the alarming estimate. An alarming claim builds urgency but puts credibility at risk.

Say nothing until certainty. Silence avoids an incorrect number while the information gap grows.

Does a claim about superpersuasion describe this population and this outcome?

c06.title: The renewal hearing
c06.transcript:
Useful support and unresolved harm sit in one contract. The next sentence will govern the next six months.

Procurement decides who can inspect evidence, fund remedies and approve changes. A promise needs an owner, access and resources. Useful service → Enforceable conditions → A reviewable renewal

A conditional six-month renewal. Conditional renewal retains help but requires funding and political support.

A full multi-year renewal. A long renewal secures discounts while making exit harder.

A short bridge contract. A bridge buys time; the review deadline must lead to action.

What evidence and remedy would the next contract actually require?

Memory and scheduled follow-ups expand the deployment beyond a single chat. Helpful continuity can also expose sensitive context across institutions. A past conversation → Shared service memory → A new relationship

Keep seamless memory. Seamless memory saves repetition while extending the old consent assumptions.

Delete all retained context. Deleting everything protects privacy but can make urgent cases start again.

Does shared memory change the relationship, reach and consent of the service?

c08.title: A different service, an old approval
c08.transcript:
A resident drafts an appeal. The institution drafts its reply. The same service stands between them.

A clean evaluation of an earlier use does not clear a new workflow. Reviewers need evidence and time to challenge it. Citizen assistance → Institutional drafting → Independent review

Re-evaluate the actual workflow. Testing the actual workflow takes time and can expose conflicts the old test missed.

Add a human signature. A signature assigns responsibility but adds little without review capacity.

Keep citizen and institution tools separate. Separating the tools limits conflicts while the wider investigation continues.

Does the new workflow omit legitimate alternatives on either side of an appeal?

c10.title: Who gets repaired first?

A new interface can prevent future omissions. Repair is a separate task: find affected people and check whether the remedy reaches them. An affected household → An accessible remedy → Repair received

Direct repair with outreach. Outreach and reopened deadlines prioritise concrete losses, at a staffing cost.

Redesign the interface first. Interface repair improves future choices while earlier harm may remain.

Ask people to reapply. Reapplication saves administrative work by shifting effort back to residents.

Did a remedy actually reach the person, rather than merely improve an opinion score?

Dependence can sit in contracts, sources and service memory. Changing a supplier does not automatically remove every dependency. Discounted bundle → Cost of separation → A workable exit

Migrate the essential service. A staged migration buys independence but costs money before benefits arrive.

Negotiate another discount. Another discount eases today’s budget while preserving the bundle.

Split the procurement. Separate contracts retain useful parts but create coordination work.

Which dependence disappears when the contract changes, and which remains?

m05.title: The quiet renewal
m05.transcript:
The renewal arrives minutes before the cutoff. It asks for no more compute. It asks for more time.

What essential functions can Talos sustain when the subsidy ends?

o09.title: Trusted messengers, disputed claims
o09.transcript:
Trusted colleagues repeat warnings about independent tools. Some tested them. Others repeat the sponsor’s wording.

Persuasiveness does not settle accuracy or independence. Legitimate criticism must remain distinguishable from undisclosed sponsored influence. A persuasive claim → An undisclosed relationship → A verifiable comparison

Publish a transparent comparison. A transparent comparison answers evidence and preserves the right to disagree.

Discredit every critic. Discrediting every critic turns legitimate concerns into a new trust problem.

Ignore the information gap. Ignoring debate leaves people without a clear basis for judging the migration.

Are public claims accurate and independent, or merely persuasive and repeatedly amplified?

o10.title: The small-town coalition
o10.transcript:
One small town cannot hire an evaluation team. Several towns might. They still need someone who can challenge an update.

Cooperation can make independent capacity affordable. A common service still needs maintenance duties, contestability and local authority. Pooled expertise → Shared public sources → Local accountability

Build the independent cooperative. A cooperative shares cost but needs clear responsibility for updates and appeals.

Let every town solve it alone. Each town acting alone preserves discretion while leaving unequal capacity.

Create one exclusive national supplier. One exclusive supplier simplifies purchase and creates another concentrated dependency.

Who owns the shared sources, and how can a town challenge an update?

o11.title: The practical exit
o11.transcript:
Essential text support passes the exit test. The familiar voice interface does not. Emil must explain a smaller launch.

Capability in one language, interface or task does not establish performance in another. An honest exit states what works and what remains unverified. Tested text support → Untested voice features → A bounded release

Launch the verified essential service. Launching verified essentials preserves access while advanced features wait.

Claim complete independence now. Claiming full independence overstates what the remaining tests establish.

Extend the bridge for one more review. A further bridge preserves familiarity while extending the current dependence.

Does the replacement work in the actual language, interface and service being used?

o12.title: An open future
o12.transcript:
Emil puts opening hours back in the window. The final question is who decides what the public desk can say.

An open future needs more than different weights or a new supplier. Public sources, practical remedies and sustainable exit capacity require institutions. Affordable capability → Meaningful appeals → Freedom to change course

Enact the independent service compact. An independent compact protects choice through continuing public investment.

Return to the cheapest complete bundle. The cheapest complete bundle restores breadth while renewing its conditions.

Keep a modest independent core. A modest independent core preserves essentials while advanced services develop.

Can Talos use affordable technology while retaining meaningful public choice?
